papers.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: A Validity Audit of Tool-Calling Evaluation
papers.claim: Tool-calling evaluation can contain evaluator-human disagreement and repeated-run variance that alter capability conclusions.

hypothesis: A single aggregate or model-judge score conceals release-relevant disagreements among task completion, side effects, evidence validity, and process quality.
null_hypothesis: A single score agrees sufficiently with component labels and repeated judging to support the same release decisions.
independent_variable: Collapsed evaluation score versus independently labeled component dimensions with deterministic, human, and repeated model-judge signals.

environment.network_justification: A named model judge and any human-labeling workflow will be selected before preregistration.

variants.name: control
variants.description: Collapsed score or single judge result.

variants.name: treatment
variants.description: Decomposed deterministic, human, and repeated judge labels.

randomness.justification: The same named model judge must be repeated under frozen settings.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Retain every dimension whose disagreement changes a release decision and preserve a human-audited sample for later comparisons.

evaluator.rubric: Two blinded human passes, deterministic checks, and repeated model judging label the same trace dimensions independently.
